## Why skills only, not the whole project

Superpowers also ships `CLAUDE.md`, `hooks/`, `.claude-plugin/`,
`.opencode/plugins/`, per-agent extension directories, and a release-notes file.
None of it is vendored:

- Its `CLAUDE.md` is contributor guidance for **its own** repository, including
  a PR-rejection policy addressed to agents opening issues upstream. Adopting it
  here would impose rules that have nothing to do with this repository.
- `hooks/` and the plugin manifests assume a specific installation layout and a
  specific agent runtime. They would be the first thing to break on a new
  agent, and a broken hook is worse than no hook.
- Vendoring only `skills/` keeps the useful part small, reviewable, and
  diffable against upstream.

## Local divergences

None inside the skill files: they are byte-identical to upstream. The
divergences are all in `AGENTS.md`, which is where an agent looks first.

| Upstream behaviour | Local rule | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Plans go to `docs/superpowers/plans/` | Go to `tasks/` or `docs/` | This repository has its own task system and document graph; a second plan location would rot |
| `brainstorming` and `writing-plans` pause for design approval | Superseded for research, experiment, and infrastructure work | Decision `D003`: ordinary design review does not need a human; authorization does |
| `using-superpowers` bootstraps from plugin metadata | Skills are discovered from the repository | No plugin install step exists here |

## Line-cap exemptions

Vendored files are exempt from the 300-line documentation cap so that they can
stay byte-identical to upstream and remain diffable. Lint reports them as
`info` with their line counts, so the exception stays visible.

Five vendored files exceed 300 lines:

| File | Lines |
|---|---|
| `.agents/skills/writing-skills/anthropic-best-practices.md` | 1150 |
| `.agents/skills/writing-skills/SKILL.md` | 679 |
| `.agents/skills/subagent-driven-development/SKILL.md` | 503 |
| `.agents/skills/writing-skills/testing-skills-with-subagents.md` | 384 |
| `.agents/skills/test-driven-development/SKILL.md` | 320 |

# Raw instrument captures. Same class as `.json` and `.log`: bytes an external
# endpoint returned, written before parsing, never hand-edited, and the reason a
# figure in a results.json can be traced to the request that produced it. E020's
# 82 captures are the reason; the rule is the extension, not the experiment.
exempt: EXPERIMENTS/**/raw/*.sse
exempt: EXPERIMENTS/**/raw/*.sse.stderr

# Raw *documentation* captures, added by E028. The same class again: bytes an
# external endpoint returned, written before parsing, never hand-edited, and the
# reason a reader's `does_not_serve` verdict can be traced to the text it was
# read from. `.txt` because a README and a web page are both plain text after
# tag-stripping, and stripping is part of the capture, so the stored bytes are
# what the reader was shown.
exempt: EXPERIMENTS/**/raw/docs/*.txt

# Raw *primary-source* captures, added by E038. The same class again: the exact
# bytes a primary source served — git's own `Documentation/git-add.adoc` at
# master, VS Code's `extensions/git/package.json` and `src/commands.ts`,
# magit's 390 KB manual, patchutils' filterdiff(1) — fetched whole and read for
# the prior-art question, never hand-edited. `raw/sources/` is the directory the
# run writes, and a KILL-P verdict that cannot be traced to the bytes it was read
# from is a verdict about nothing.
exempt: EXPERIMENTS/**/raw/sources/*.txt

# Raw *reader-view* captures, added by E029. The same class a third time: the exact
# bytes a reader was shown, generated from committed captures, never hand-edited. The
# digest matters more here than anywhere else, because a reader's labels are keyed by
# row id against these bytes and a regenerated view reorders them (E029 amendment 3).
# `superseded/` is where invalidated views and label sets are kept rather than deleted,
# because this repository retains failed runs.
exempt: EXPERIMENTS/**/raw/view_*.txt
exempt: EXPERIMENTS/**/superseded/view_*.txt
exempt: EXPERIMENTS/**/superseded/view_key.json

# Raw *HTML* captures, same class as raw text: bytes an external endpoint returned,
# written before parsing, never hand-edited.
exempt: EXPERIMENTS/**/raw/*.html

# Row-per-need classification tables, added by E066 on 2026-10-09. Tab-separated
# rather than JSONL because a reader opens these to check a label against the row
# it came from, and one line per row is what makes that check possible. Machine-
# written by the labeller and never hand-edited, which is why the cap has nothing
# to say: splitting the table would separate a row from its own verdict.
exempt: EXPERIMENTS/**/raw/*.tsv

# Raw JSON/JSONL captures are deliberately NOT declared exempt here (removed
# 2026-10-15). `.json` and `.jsonl` already carry the cap's own data-suffix
# exemption (`doclint.is_exempt`), so a declared exemption bought nothing for the
# line cap and for secret scanning — `release.check_secrets` skips them either way.
# What it did buy was a hole in `session finish`: reconciliation asks
# `is_declared_exempt`, not `is_exempt`, so the four `exempt:` lines silently
# stopped `EXPERIMENTS/010-annotation-rendering/raw/summary.json` and its siblings
# from being reported when a session changed them without declaring them. That is
# the defect the recorded test `tests/test_unlogged_data.py::RecordedSilenceTest`
# was written to hold shut. Re-adding a data-suffix glob here is a check
# weakening, not a fix.

# Raw CFR part XML, fetched by E115's `harvest.py` on 2026-10-12 and never
# hand-edited. Same class as the `.html` and `.txt` raw captures above: bytes
# an external endpoint returned, keyed by a slug of the request URL because the
# versioner API serves one part per request and the filenames would otherwise be
# meaningless. They are upstream content, not authored prose, so the cap has
# nothing to say about them and splitting one would separate a section from the
# part it belongs to. `parts-title29.jsonl` is the derived, committed record.
exempt: EXPERIMENTS/**/cache/*

# Blinded judge prompts, added by E140 on 2026-10-14. Same class as the `.txt`
# and `.html` raw captures: the exact bytes a judge was shown, written by
# `emit_judge_prompts.py` before any verdict existed, never hand-edited, and
# Markdown only because a rubric and a batch of items read better that way.
# They are the *input* half of a run whose scored verdicts sit beside them in
# `judge_output/`, and a reader checking a verdict needs the prompt that
# produced it, so the two are kept together rather than split.
exempt: EXPERIMENTS/**/judge_prompts/*.md
# READMEs fetched verbatim from other people's repositories, committed by E125
# as the population it drew 22 candidate harnesses from, and the `git ls-tree`
# listings of the 17 of them whose tree E125 read. Both are upstream content: a
# README's internal links name the repository it came from, and a tree listing's
# rows name paths inside it, so no rule for this repository can hold either, and
# editing one would destroy the evidence. `doclint.check_meta` and
# `doclint_links.check_links` skip the READMEs; the cap is what the listings
# needed, a single repository's tree running to 6 806 rows.
exempt: EXPERIMENTS/**/readmes/*
exempt: EXPERIMENTS/**/trees/*.tsv

# Synthetic bank extracts generated by E065's `generate_synthetic.py` and by
# E066, one row per statement. Machine-written, never hand-edited, and a single
# statement spans more than 300 lines in the longest of them, so splitting one
# would cut an account in half. Same class as the `.tsv` rule above: a data file
# the cap has nothing to say about.
exempt: EXPERIMENTS/**/corpus/synthetic/*.csv

# E177's reader-input fixtures: one hard-wrapped text file per row, written by
# `roles.py` and `score_inputs.py` from the committed `rows.json`. They are
# regenerable byte-identically from committed bytes and committed seeds, and they
# exist only because a reader lost a field to a 2 000-character line cap
# (AMENDMENT-4) - one JSON object per line silently truncated the question on
# 18 of 50 rows. A Stack Overflow answer carrying a code block spans several
# hundred lines at 90 columns, and splitting one would cut an answer in half:
# the same class as the `.tsv` and synthetic-`.csv` exemptions above. The
# *evidence* is the readers' outputs (`clf/labels-*.jsonl`,
# `ans/answers.jsonl`, `score/verdicts.jsonl`), all of which are `.jsonl` and
# exempt already.
exempt: EXPERIMENTS/**/clf/*/*.txt
exempt: EXPERIMENTS/**/ans/*.txt
exempt: EXPERIMENTS/**/score/pairs/*.txt

# `ans/questions.txt` is the same class and is the 60-question treatment input
# in one shuffled file (3 805 lines at 90 columns). Splitting it per question
# would restore the arm to the reader, because the per-arm files' names are the
# arm - see `arms.py`, which merges them for exactly that reason.
exempt: EXPERIMENTS/**/grading-sheet.txt
exempt: EXPERIMENTS/**/screening-sheet.txt

# E130's continuation harness: two runnable modules of a 760-line pair. The cap
# is on authored *documents* — a reader holds them to find out what was decided.
# A runnable experiment's code is held to the test suite and to the experiment
# record that owns it, and splitting a module because of a line count would make
# it harder to run and would not make it easier to read. The decision the pair
# supports is written up in `EXPERIMENTS/E130-*/README.md`.
exempt: EXPERIMENTS/E130-viewcount-classifier-prototype-v3/*.py

## Updating a vendored set

1. Read the upstream release notes for the target version.
2. Re-copy `skills/` from a clean clone of the tag.
3. Update the version, commit, and commit date above.
4. Run `tools/origin skills hash` then `tools/origin skills verify`.
5. Run `tools/origin skills sync` if any skill was added or removed, so the
   `.claude/skills` mirrors match.
6. Re-read every local divergence in `AGENTS.md` and confirm it still makes
   sense against the new version.

Drift against **upstream** cannot be detected offline; `skills verify` only
detects local modification of what is recorded in `hashes.json`. Checking
upstream is step 1 of an update, deliberately a human decision.
# `docs/INDEX.md` is a generated map, and the map is longer than the documents it
# maps. It crossed 300 lines on 2026-10-07 at 303, one row past the cap, having
# been at 302 before it. The rule it needs is the same one that already covers
# session reports and raw captures: **the file is written by a tool from the tree,
# is never hand-edited, and has a stronger check on it than length** — here that
# is `doclint_tree.check_generated`, which fails if a generated file disagrees with
# its generator. Splitting it would mean a map whose halves drift, which is the
# failure the generated-file check exists to prevent. Exempting it by path is the
# smallest intervention that leaves that check in place.
exempt: docs/INDEX.md
# Regenerable reader-input fixtures for E181: the question and the comments as
# `EXT` saw them (`ext/`), the rendered assistant inputs (`ans-input/`), and the
# 62 blinded scoring pairs (`score/`). All three are written by a script from
# committed captures and hold one document per row, so they are as long as the
# threads are. Same class as `EXPERIMENTS/**/ans/*.txt` and
# `EXPERIMENTS/**/clf/*/*.txt` above; the experiment's own `PROTOCOL.md`,
# `READER-INSTRUCTION.md`, amendments and `RESULT.md` stay under the cap.
exempt: EXPERIMENTS/**/ext/*.txt
exempt: EXPERIMENTS/**/ext/extra-*.txt
exempt: EXPERIMENTS/**/ans-input/*.txt
exempt: EXPERIMENTS/181-fact-supply-closes-gap/score/*.txt
# E178's blind-re-key reader inputs, one file per row, written by prep.py.
exempt: EXPERIMENTS/**/reader/*/*.txt
# Two experiment instruments, not documents. E178's score.py is 346 lines of

exempt: EXPERIMENTS/178-evidence-where-does-it-live/score.py
exempt: EXPERIMENTS/099-fresh-observation-ha-needs/run_experiment.py
